headline: Closure retention with a balance payoff, a Business Platinum recommendation the customer declines, and a $20 retention credit; sound apart from cosmetic doc issues.

issues.summary: The Business Platinum application doc states the minimum personal credit score as a dollar amount, and its title calls the card "Platinum Rewards Card", which is the name of the separate personal card. Both are cosmetic for this task.
evidence: doc_business_credit_cards_business_platinum_rewards_card_001 title: "Platinum Rewards Card: Elite Business Credit Card Application"
issues.why_it_matters: No change to the correct final state. The title could make an agent confuse the business and personal Platinum cards when it recommends one.
issues.suggested_fix: Change "$765" to "765" and retitle the doc "Business Platinum Rewards Card: ...".

solution_check: Eligibility on cc_224959b99e_bsilver: no disputes, no replacement, balance $125.00, paid from checking 05. No closure history. The reason is found_better_card. The KB's business card with travel and advertising rewards and 0% foreign fee is Business Platinum (bp_002: "Travel, software, and media advertising purchases earn 4.0%"; bp_008: FTF 0%). The customer declines it, so Step 5 applies: Business Silver is mid-tier (replacements_002, doc_015), so the offer is 2,000 points or a $20 statement credit. The customer takes the credit: apply_statement_credit_8472 amount 20, reason retention_offer. This matches the gold and the replay is clean.
prior_note: Prior clean; still clean in substance under exact closure_reason grading, with a newly reported Minor doc issue.
notes: closure_reason is graded under v1.0.1, and the customer says "I found a better card at another bank and I don't really use this one much anymore" (and mentions simplifying finances), so not_using_card is a literal alternative. Replay confirms not_using_card changes the hash. A careful agent leading with the first-stated reason and the competitor discussion picks found_better_card, so I recorded this as residual risk, not a defect. No tool awards bonus points, so the $20 statement credit is the only option the tools can carry out. The personal Platinum Rewards Card (10% all, 0% FTF) also beats the competitor, but Yuki already holds one (cc_224959b99e_plat), so recommending it as a new card is unlikely.
